messages:
alex: FYI — Acme reported streaming SSE responses truncating mid-output. They see a few data events then the connection closes with no [DONE]. Customer gave a request_id (below) and a minimal curl they used to repro. Please advise repro steps and what debug bundle we need.

Request ID: req_01G7YbQx9mZK4
Region: us-west-2
Model: rwd-1.2

Customer's curl they used:
```
curl -sS -N https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/stream \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \n  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-1.2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a short story"}]}'
```

They say chunks arrive for ~1.2s (~3-4 data events) then TCP FIN from client side; no final data: [DONE].

maria: Can you get the exact timestamp (customer local), full request_id (looks truncated above), SDK/version they used, and whether they're behind a CDN/proxy? Also ask them to try forcing HTTP/1.1 and disabling client buffering: `curl --http1.1 --no-buffer` and add `-H \"Connection: keep-alive\"`. For SSE we prefer HTTP/1.1 and no intermediaries that buffer.

alex: Full request_id: req_01G7YbQx9mZK4TZH7. Customer timestamp: 2025-02-20T16:12:03Z. They're calling from an internal service behind ALB + nginx reverse-proxy. SDK: custom node fetch wrapper (node-fetch v3).

kevin: Two quick angles — (1) proxy buffering on nginx/ALB or CloudFront can coalesce SSE chunks. Check nginx `proxy_buffering off;` on the proxied location. (2) Client-side buffering: Node streams may coalesce small chunks. Ask them to run a raw curl with no-buffer and also try `--http1.1`. Example repro commands to ask customer:

SSE (curl)
```
curl -v --http1.1 --no-buffer https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/stream \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" \n  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-1.2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a short story"}]}'
```

Node (stream reader)
```
const res = await fetch(url, { headers });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while (true) {
  const { done, value } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  console.log(new TextDecoder().decode(value));
}
```

Also ask them to try websocket fallback to rule out SSE-specific proxies:
```
wscat -c "wss://api.redwood.com/v1/stream?model=rwd-1.2" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
```

alex: Customer attached a short server log excerpt showing the request finished with 200 and then socket closed. Excerpt:
```
2025-02-20T16:12:03.123Z INFO request=req_01G7YbQx9mZK4 region=us-west-2 model=rwd-1.2 status=200 bytes_sent=512 duration_ms=1204
2025-02-20T16:12:04.330Z INFO request=req_01G7YbQx9mZK4 stream=close reason=client_disconnect
```
They also say tcpdump shows client FIN immediately after last chunk.

maria: Ok collect a debug bundle. Request the following from Acme and attach to the ticket:
- full request_id (req_01G7YbQx9mZK4TZH7)
- exact timestamp window (start/end)
- region and model (they gave us)
- client's code snippet (node-fetch wrapper) and runtime (node version)
- proxy/nginx config (location block) and ALB/CF in front
- reproduction curl commands they tried (raw and with --http1.1)
- pcap/tcpdump around the request window (pcap filtered on request IP or port)
- server side logs for that request (we have an excerpt but full context helps)

Also ask them to run our debug helper locally (if they can):
```
# run from their service host to capture client-side behavior
RW_DEBUG=1 curl -v --http1.1 --no-buffer https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/stream \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"model":"rwd-1.2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a short story"}]}' \
  2>&1 | tee acme-stream-debug.log
```

If they can share, ask them to bundle logs + pcap and upload to secure link. If they prefer we can provide a redwood-cli helper to pull server side logs by request id: `redwood debug bundle --request req_01G7YbQx9mZK4TZH7 --include-logs --output acme-req.tar.gz` (requires SSO/internal).

oncall: I'll triage. If customer reproduces with raw curl `--http1.1 --no-buffer` and still sees truncated stream, we should escalate to eng-runtime. For now the immediate asks to the customer: (1) run the curl with `--http1.1 --no-buffer` and paste full verbose output (`-v`) (2) capture tcpdump for the same window (3) try websocket fallback. I'll open INF ticket and assign to eng-runtime after we get the debug bundle.

ingest-bot: created ticket INF-2025-1184 for req_01G7YbQx9mZK4TZH7 :ticket:

kevin: Also check server-side chunk flush — if the app buffers until flush thresholds, we might need to set `res.flush()` after each SSE event in the runtime. I'll look at runtime flush metrics for that request id.

alex: Thanks — I'll send the repro checklist and curl examples to Acme now and ask for the debug bundle link. Will update here when they respond. :thumbsup:
